timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Did you know that black holes are like cosmic vacuum cleaners, sucking in everything that comes near enough to them?
These mysterious objects are formed when a massive star collapses under its own gravity, creating a region in space where gravity is so intense that nothing, not even light, can escape its grasp.
Imagine a place with a laws of physics as we know them break down to a point of infinite density and zero volume called a singularity.
That's what lies at the heart of every black hole in our universe.

Black holes come in many different sizes, from stellar black holes, which can be a few times more massive than our own sun, to supermassive black holes that can have millions or even billions of times the massive r sun.
While black holes may seem like cosmic destroyers, they do play a vital role in shaping our universe.
They can influence the formation and evolution of galaxies, and their powerful jets of energy can be observed across vast cosmic distances.
So the next time you gaze up at the sky, marvel at the cosmic vacuum cleaners that are black holes.
